notes: Re-measured 2026-07-23 at 9.85ms/test (376s across 38198 tests). Three full-suite runs of the same tree this session disagreed wildly -- 375s/9.85ms, 472s/12.54ms (the prior cold pre-push gate), and 742s/19.42ms -- a ~2x wall-clock spread driven by machine load, not code cost. The baseline deliberately takes the LEAST-loaded run (9.85ms) scaled to the current count so the 1.3 ratio still catches a genuine per-test regression rather than being padded up to absorb noise; the trade-off is that a heavily-loaded cold push can trip the rail, which is a machine-load signal to re-run, not a slowdown to 'fix' by deleting tests. Test count grew 32489 -> 38198 (+17.6%%) over ~6 weeks of feature work (loop-A/B, OpenHands loop, memory tail, governed deploy); that count growth is mechanical scale drift. Per-test cost is not up from this branch's changes -- deferring litellm out of app construction lowers it -- so the rail measures real work, not import overhead.
